title: Seat Reservation Manager
prompt:
The classic version of this problem defines a `SeatManager` class initialized with an integer `n` (seats numbered 1 to n, all initially available), exposing `reserve()` (reserves and returns the smallest-numbered available seat) and `unreserve(seatNumber)` (makes that seat available again). Since this test harness calls a single pure function per test case rather than exercising a stateful object, we adapt it: implement `seat_reservation_manager(n, operations)`.

`operations` is a list where each entry is either `["reserve"]` or `["unreserve", seatNumber]`, applied in order. For every `"reserve"` operation, record the seat number that was reserved (the smallest-numbered seat currently available). Return a list of these recorded seat numbers, one per `"reserve"` operation, in the order they occurred.

examples.explanation: Reserve->1, Reserve->2, Unreserve 2 (2 free again), Reserve->2, Reserve->3, Reserve->4, Reserve->5, Unreserve 5.

constraints: For unreserve, 1 <= seatNumber <= n, and the seat is currently reserved
hints: You always need the smallest available seat number, and seats can become available again out of order after being unreserved.
A min-heap of currently-available seat numbers gives O(log n) access to the smallest available seat at any time.

Rather than pre-populating the heap with all n seats up front (which still works but uses more initial memory/time than necessary), you can lazily track the next never-yet-used seat with a counter, only pushing explicitly unreserved seats onto the heap; reserve pulls from the heap if it's non-empty, otherwise takes the next fresh seat from the counter.

solution.approach: Track a counter `next_fresh` for the smallest seat number never yet reserved, and a min-heap holding seats that were previously reserved and later freed via unreserve. Any freed seat was, by definition, already reserved earlier, so it must be numbered below `next_fresh`; that means the heap's minimum (when non-empty) is always the correct next seat to hand out, and only when the heap is empty do we fall back to `next_fresh`, incrementing it afterward. On unreserve, push the freed seat number onto the heap so it becomes available again. This avoids pre-allocating a heap of all n seats up front.
solution.timeComplexity: O(m log m) for m operations
